claim: In 2016 Andrew Poelstra gave the first public talk about Mimblewimble at Scaling Bitcoin.

claim: Andrew Poelstra explained that Mimblewimble's key trick is a quirk of confidential-transaction algebra that lets transactions be cut through, so intermediate steps can be deleted from the chain.
speaker: Andrew Poelstra
quote: it exploits a quirk of confidential transactions algebra to allow transactions to be cut through.
title: Monero Monitor: Mimblewimble with Andrew Poelstra

claim: Andrew Poelstra said a Mimblewimble chain can be treated as one enormous transaction, so a verifier only needs to check each original transaction's signature.

quote: In Mimblewimble you can take the blockchain essentially treat it as one enormous transaction
title: Monero Monitor: Mimblewimble with Andrew Poelstra

claim: Andrew Poelstra explained that a verifier of a Mimblewimble chain needs only a single digital signature per original transaction rather than replaying every historic transaction.
speaker: Andrew Poelstra
quote: All they need to check is for each original transaction just a single digital signature.
title: Monero Monitor: Mimblewimble with Andrew Poelstra

claim: Andrew Poelstra said Monero was based on Bytecoin, which he called a bizarre pre-mine scam, and that Monero's ring signature came from it.

title: Monero Monitor: Mimblewimble with Andrew Poelstra

claim: Andrew Poelstra said there was a lot of evidence that the signature on the December 2012 white paper by Nicholas Van Saberhagen was faked, with software that did not exist in 2012.

quote: there's a whole lot of evidence that the signature on that white paper was faked and that it was signed with software that didn't even exist in 2012.
title: Monero Monitor: Mimblewimble with Andrew Poelstra

claim: Andrew Poelstra described OWAS, a one-way aggregate signature paper published on Bitcoin Talk in September 2013 under the pseudonym Horace, as a direct precursor to Mimblewimble.
